title: State of Punjab v. Mohar Singh

content.caseIdentity: State of Punjab v. Mohar Singh, AIR 1955 SC 84
content.facts: The East Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Act, 1948 repealed a 1947 Ordinance without an express savings clause in the new enactment. The respondent was prosecuted after the repeal for an offence committed during the currency of the Ordinance.
questionsBeforeCourt: How a repeal without an express savings clause operates, and the scope of Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 in preserving liabilities and investigations.
content.ratioDecidendi: Whenever there is a repeal of an enactment, the consequences laid down in Section 6 of the General Clauses Act follow unless, as the section itself says, a different intention appears. The court must look to the provisions of the new Act to see whether they indicate a different intention and whether the previous rights and liabilities are preserved.
content.holding: Held that prosecution for acts committed under the repealed Ordinance was preserved by Section 6 of the General Clauses Act.
content.relevance: Leading authority on the interpretation of statutory repeal and savings provisions, controlling the operation of Section 531 BNSS.
